question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: The panel on review 2026-10-03-markdown-table-cell-blocks (opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol) found that its target rebuilt list properties in the runtime, missed main's task markup, overclaimed losslessness, misread D8 against the shipped docs and let the ledger count an unrelated design as progress. This review corrects the target before any plan.
requirements: Preserve representable Markdown meaning in GFM table cells; diagnose intentional or unsupported loss and obey lossPolicy.
A GFM row stays on one line: no cell content may write a raw newline into the row.
Features own their mappings: the List feature builds list paragraphs; the Markdown runtime owns intrinsic syntax only.
Keep Markdown parsing DOM-free and keep the selective registered-tag grammar; raw HTML that no mapping accepts stays literal with a lossless warning under every policy, as the Markdown docs state.

Read the Markdown Plate writes on main: since PR 5139 it writes cell lists as inline
    ,
      and
    1. HTML, task items with a leading , and cell breaks as
      . Markdown is serialized data, and the 2026-09-28 dialect already gated adoption on reading legacy Plate output; the verdict also holds on GFM renderability and losslessness alone.
evidenceReuse: Reused the first record's probes and law; read main's merged encoder (main-tableRules.ts at a8607621c0); saved output for every HTML probe; checked the Markdown docs raw-HTML contract; reread the ledger rule that lets a retained review govern progress.
summary:
Pursue, with a corrected target. On next, a table cell holding list paragraphs refuses and the refusal cascades through the row and the table: under the default lossPolicy reject the whole serialize fails and copy writes no text/markdown, and under allow the whole table disappears. A break inside a cell paragraph becomes a space with no diagnostic, and a trailing break writes a raw newline into the row, which corrupts the table on re-read. Main writes cell lists as inline HTML, which next reads as literal text. The target is a runtime-owned syntax transform at the mdast level: inside a tableCell, a one-line
    /
      /
    1. run with an optional leading becomes an mdast list and listItem (checked from the input), so the List feature's existing decoder builds the paragraphs; on write, the mdast list the runtime already builds renders as that one-line HTML inside the cell, cell breaks render as
      from the same owner, and an unrepresentable cell keeps its column as an empty cell with a lossy diagnostic instead of dropping the table. What an mdast list cannot hold (listStyle, indent gaps, image items) keeps its existing D18 report. Two paragraphs and an in-paragraph break both read back as one paragraph with a newline; the design documents that folding or reports it as a warning, and never leaves it silent.

callSites.current: No public call changes. Today the table cell markdown.encode runs encode(children); a list paragraph group returns an mdast list, so the cell refuses, the row and the table refuse in turn, and serialize fails under reject or drops the table under allow. The cell encoder spreads paragraph children into the row, so a break becomes a space and a trailing break writes a raw newline. On parse, <ul><li> in a cell stays literal text with one lossless warning per tag.
callSites.proposed:
No public call changes. Parse: a runtime tree pass beside the tableCell demotion rewrites a cell's
    /
      /
    1. / html run into mdast list and listItem; the List decoder builds the paragraphs and the table decoder keeps them as block children. Serialize: the runtime renders the mdast list it already builds as one-line inline HTML inside a tableCell, writes cell breaks as
      , and the cell encoder stops refusing lists; a cell it still cannot represent writes an empty cell with a lossy diagnostic so the row and table survive.

reconciliation.reason: Same verdict with a corrected target: a syntax transform at the mdast level instead of a runtime list decoder, task checkboxes, a narrowed refusal cascade, runtime-owned cell breaks, D8 settled by the shipped docs contract, and reading main's output tied to serialized data. It also stops this question inheriting the format-mapping design as progress.

reconciliation.reason: Reopens the scope question for table cells only: block content and raw HTML inside a GFM cell. The selective registered-tag recognizer, DOM-free parsing and strict final parsing stay.

reconciliation.question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Reopens D6 for table cells. D8's lossPolicy clause is superseded by the shipped contract in the Markdown docs: raw HTML no mapping accepts stays literal with a lossless warning under every policy. D9 and the other decisions stay.

reconciliation.question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
reconciliation.reason: Same as the design record: D6 reopens for table cells; D8's lossPolicy clause is superseded by the shipped docs contract; dispatch semantics and the attribute codec stay.

alternatives: Keep refusing: loses. It is honest about loss but fails every export of a document with a list in any cell and drops the whole table under allow.

Flatten list paragraphs into paragraphs joined by
with markdown-property-omitted warnings: viable fallback that keeps text and explicit loss, but it drops structure GFM viewers render from HTML.

Runtime decoder that rebuilds list paragraphs from a cell's HTML (the first record's target): superseded. It duplicates the List feature's decode, including restart and start logic, which is how main's table rules drifted.

Reuse the feature HTML mappings to write and read HTML in cells: Stop. The Markdown mapping contract exposes no HTML encode or decode, although every editor compiles the HTML artifact. Saved probes show HTML serialize writes one <ul>/<ol> per item with data-* attributes and margin styles and leaves | and raw newlines inside <li>, each of which breaks a GFM row; HTML parse needs a DOM that Markdown parsing avoids and ignores <input type="checkbox"> task markup.

Register ul, ol and li as Plate tags: Stop. Lists are native Markdown outside cells, so registering them would claim raw list HTML everywhere; D9 also demotes registered block tags inside a tableCell.

Runtime mdast-level transform between a cell's inline HTML list run and an mdast list, with checkbox support, runtime-owned cell breaks and a narrowed refusal cascade: Pursue. The List and Table mappings keep their ownership, D18 accounting is reused, GFM viewers render the output and main's output reads back.
proofLimits: Source inspection, headless probes against the platejs dist built on 2026-10-02 and the next source, and main's merged encoder read at a8607621c0. Every probe cited has saved output. No browser, clipboard, GitHub rendering check, package suite or Benchmark run, and no prototype of the mdast-level transform. Reading main's output is argued from its encoder and a hand-written cell, not a corpus of main exports. Evidence lives in gitignored docs/plans/artifacts, as in earlier records of this scope.
